=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:emit_run_budget_gate_note function | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The `printf | tee -a ...` pipeline can abort the reviewer run under `set -euo pipefail` if `tee` fails.
  WHY: A write/permission/disk error turns a best-effort diagnostic into a hard failure that can discard reviewer/editor work.
- scripts/watchdog_helpers.sh:174-175 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `emit_run_budget_gate_note` still writes through `tee -a "${budget_log_file}" >&2`, so I/O failures can abort the reviewer run.
  WHY: Under caller `set -euo pipefail`, a failed append can stop the run and lose findings.
- scripts/watchdog_helpers.sh:codex_run_budget_export function | severity=medium | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The helper can export arbitrary initializer `key=value` lines instead of only the intended budget env vars.
  WHY: Malformed output can pollute the environment with unintended variables.
- scripts/watchdog_helpers.sh:58-68 (`normalize_review_soft_deadline_minutes`) | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Zero-padded values are handled inconsistently, which can trigger duplicate warnings or mismatched normalization between workflow init and the helper.
  WHY: The raw-value warning path and the `10#` arithmetic path do not line up cleanly, so callers can see inconsistent behavior.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:editor attempt budgeting logic | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: If `codex_run_budget_remaining_secs` returns a non-numeric value, `budget_cap=$(( remaining - 120 ))` can fail under `set -euo pipefail`.
  WHY: A bad `remaining` value can abort the editor attempt and discard reviewer/editor work.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1702-1714 (editor loop) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup-buffer guard returns early without updating `remaining` or emitting `budget_summary`, so downstream state stays stale.
  WHY: Near-deadline attempts can log the skip while the emitted heartbeat and substate still claim full budget, breaking observability.
- scripts/watchdog_helpers.sh:normalize_review_soft_deadline_minutes function | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The helper’s `printf '%s\n' "${CODEX_RUN_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MINUTES}"` output is claimed to be pipeline/redirect fragile.
  WHY: Captured or redirected output may behave unexpectedly in shell consumers.
- scripts/codex_heartbeat.sh:148-166 and scripts/codex_stall_guard.sh:216-234 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_budget_suffix_for_now()` is duplicated across both scripts, so future changes must be made in two places.
  WHY: The two implementations can diverge and silently drop or alter budget fields.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The PR must ensure that the new soft-deadline budget contract is robust against runtime failures and does not introduce new failure modes that discard reviewer/editor work.
  expected_change_site: All modified scripts and workflows should include appropriate error handling and validation to prevent aborts due to non-critical diagnostics.
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  EVIDENCE: The LAST RUN DIFF and PR DIFF do not include error handling or validation for the new budget contract in several places, leaving the contract vulnerable to runtime failures.
- requirement: "The heartbeat line includes elapsed and remaining budget data in a grep-friendly additive format."
  expected_change_site: CODEX_HEARTBEAT output in both codex_heartbeat.sh and codex_stall_guard.sh (and callers)
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: LAST_RUN_DIFF shows the suffix is appended, but the duplicated helper and missing unified test coverage mean the format is not contractually pinned across both paths; the final PR still has two independent implementations.
- requirement: "Wire shared budget-accounting helpers into the workflow and the reviewer/editor entrypoints so every major phase can ask whether it is still allowed to start."
  expected_change_site: All major review_autofix phases (reviewers, editor, stall guard) + orchestration if reused
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: Wiring is present in reviewer/editor/heartbeat/stall-guard but the `codex_run_budget_phase_may_start` call in review_run_reviewers.sh is only advisory (logs `may_start=`) and does not yet enforce a hard stop; acceptance criteria explicitly forbid a new red/failing terminal path in this foundation phase, but later phases (per original issue #3710) will need the enforcement path.

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- File: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh
  Code: emit_run_budget_gate_note function
  Problem: The function uses `printf | tee -a ...` pipeline under `set -euo pipefail`, so a `tee` failure (e.g., missing parent dir, permission issue, full disk) will exit non-zero and abort the reviewer run, turning a best-effort diagnostic into a hard failure path.
  Runtime impact: A failing `tee` can abort the reviewer run, discarding all reviewer/editor work and failing the PR.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/watchdog_helpers.sh
  Code: codex_run_budget_export function
  Problem: The function exports any line starting with `JOB_START_EPOCH=`, `REVIEW_SOFT_DEADLINE_MINUTES=`, or `CODEX_RUN_BUDGET_*=`, but the initializer can emit arbitrary `key=value` lines (e.g., `note=ignored`). If such a line is produced, it will be incorrectly exported, potentially polluting the environment with unintended variables.
  Runtime impact: Unintended environment pollution could affect downstream scripts or cause subtle bugs.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/watchdog_helpers.sh
  Code: normalize_review_soft_deadline_minutes function
  Problem: The function uses `printf '%s\n' "${CODEX_RUN_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MINUTES}"` without a trailing newline, which can break shell pipelines or cause unexpected behavior when the output is captured or redirected.
  Runtime impact: Potential pipeline breakage or unexpected behavior in shell scripts that consume the function's output.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh
  Code: editor attempt budgeting logic
  Problem: The code computes `budget_cap=$(( remaining - 120 ))` and then checks `if [ "${budget_cap}" -le 0 ]`, but if `remaining` is not a number (e.g., empty or non-numeric), the arithmetic will fail and the script will exit non-zero under `set -euo pipefail`, aborting the editor attempt.
  Runtime impact: A non-numeric `remaining` can cause the editor attempt to fail, discarding reviewer/editor work.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: The PR must ensure that the new soft-deadline budget contract is robust against runtime failures and does not introduce new failure modes that discard reviewer/editor work.
  Expected change site: All modified scripts and workflows should include appropriate error handling and validation to prevent aborts due to non-critical diagnostics.
  Evidence of absence: The LAST RUN DIFF and PR DIFF do not include error handling or validation for the new budget contract in several places, leaving the contract vulnerable to runtime failures.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: scripts/watchdog_helpers.sh:174-175 (in `emit_run_budget_gate_note`)
  Line or code reference: `printf ... | tee -a "${budget_log_file}" >&2 || true`
  Problem: The `tee` pipeline under implicit `set -euo pipefail` (from callers like review_run_reviewers.sh) can still fail the whole reviewer run on rare I/O errors (full disk, permission, missing dir) despite the `|| true` — the `||` only guards the tee exit, but pipeline semantics and caller sourcing can propagate non-zero status.
  Why it fails at runtime: A transient write failure aborts reviewer pass, discarding all findings and preventing editor run (observed Copilot floor-tag in PR comments).
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1702-1714 (editor loop)
  Line or code reference: `budget_cap=$(( remaining - 120 )); if [ "${budget_cap}" -le 0 ]; then ... break`
  Problem: The cleanup-buffer guard correctly prevents negative `attempt_wall` but does not update `remaining` or emit `budget_summary` when the guard fires; downstream editor substate and heartbeat accounting stay stale.
  Why it fails at runtime: Near-deadline attempts log "skipping ... after reserving the 120s cleanup buffer" but the emitted heartbeat and substate still claim full budget, breaking observability for stall-guard/judge.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/watchdog_helpers.sh:58-68 (`normalize_review_soft_deadline_minutes`)
  Line or code reference: `case "${raw_value}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) ...; normalized_value="$(( 10#${raw_value} ))"`
  Problem: Zero-padded values (e.g. `0030` from env) are accepted by the `10#` arithmetic but the warning path for non-numeric is triggered only on the raw string; the test in `test_review_editor_fifo_drain.py:270` asserts no warning for `0030` but the workflow init in review_autofix.yml:1538 still emits a warning on `0030` before calling the helper.
  Why it fails at runtime: Duplicate warnings + inconsistent normalization between workflow and helper (observed in last_run editor summary).
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/codex_heartbeat.sh:148-166 and scripts/codex_stall_guard.sh:216-234
  Line or code reference: duplicated `_budget_suffix_for_now()` implementations (identical logic, different Python vs Bash).
  Problem: Duplication means any future change (e.g. handling of negative remaining, timezone, or new budget field) must be made in two places; tests only cover one path each.
  Why it fails at runtime: Divergence risk (already seen in prior autofix rounds); one path could silently drop budget fields.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "The heartbeat line includes elapsed and remaining budget data in a grep-friendly additive format."
  Expected change site: CODEX_HEARTBEAT output in both codex_heartbeat.sh and codex_stall_guard.sh (and callers)
  Evidence of absence: LAST_RUN_DIFF shows the suffix is appended, but the duplicated helper and missing unified test coverage mean the format is not contractually pinned across both paths; the final PR still has two independent implementations.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Wire shared budget-accounting helpers into the workflow and the reviewer/editor entrypoints so every major phase can ask whether it is still allowed to start."
  Expected change site: All major review_autofix phases (reviewers, editor, stall guard) + orchestration if reused
  Evidence of absence: Wiring is present in reviewer/editor/heartbeat/stall-guard but the `codex_run_budget_phase_may_start` call in review_run_reviewers.sh is only advisory (logs `may_start=`) and does not yet enforce a hard stop; acceptance criteria explicitly forbid a new red/failing terminal path in this foundation phase, but later phases (per original issue #3710) will need the enforcement path.
  SEV
